original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Prove that every rational decomposition of the seven-call profile (2,1,1,0)/(1,1,1) fails target support or has a character detecting two calls and four targets, so the profile admits no word under the cited premises.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian native alphabet. This package stays in the abelian symmetric 2-by-2 model and answers the first remaining profile of the seven-call three-frame handoff, orbit O3's representative (2,1,1,0)/(1,1,1).
bottleneck_link: Side result on the signed-frame escape. This profile still needs more than seven paid calls under the cited premises, so there is no local call-count saving and no selected-frontier change.
stop_rule: Stop after the support-or-character proof for (2,1,1,0)/(1,1,1), or after an explicit decomposition that passes both tests. Do not take the (0,1,1,1)/(1,1,2) profile or a four-frame equation.
evidence: Proof that support holds exactly for a Q frame plus a rank-one pair summing to A+2B, and that every such pair has odd reduced denominator and even c-numerator, giving a character with calls 2 and targets 4. The twelve-offset screen and the polynomial expansion are exhaustive. A 323-pair sample is corroboration only.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Substantial Cursor Grok assistance with the proof and verifier. No independent human or formal-kernel review.

open_questions.question: Does every decomposition of (0,1,1,1)/(1,1,2) fail a character or fail target support?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That is the representative of orbit O4. A decomposition passing both tests would be the first three-frame candidate word; an exclusion would close four profiles if the #7128 transport lemma is granted.
open_questions.first_step: Classify subset sums of B+Q and A+Q against residual diag(3,2), then test the surviving pairs with one character.
open_questions.blocked_by: The Q-frame argument uses residual (2,3,-1) and does not apply to diag(3,2).

open_questions.question: Do the other seven profiles of orbit O3 follow from this exclusion without citing the transport lemma as an external premise?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR #7128 states that one argument per orbit is enough, but that lemma is open and unreviewed. A direct transport would make the whole orbit unconditional.
open_questions.first_step: Apply one label map to the Q-frame decomposition and repeat Lemmas 1 and 4 in the image coordinates.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package does not prove the transport lemma.
